content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Brooks Garner's PostBrooks Garner Verified accountMarch 31 at 11:30 PM · Shared with Public ARTEMIS II MOONSHOT TOMORROW NIGHT THIS IS HISTORY.First crewed mission around the Moon in 50+ years… and you might be able to see it.Launch window: 6:24 PM to 8:24 PMThis map shows when to look Here’s the catch…If it launches EARLY, it’s still daylight and harder to see outside Florida.If it launches LATE, it gets darker and visibility improves into Georgia and the Carolinas.Clear skies = LET’S GOClouds or haze = you may miss itIf you’re in Florida, don’t even think about skipping this.Elsewhere, you’ve got a shot if skies cooperate.All reactions:3K370 comments1.5K sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Ntj Nate TheJewelerWhat would be hysterical is if NASA had millions of people standing in their yards for 3 hours only to announce APRIL FOOLS at the last minutes!2w43View all 2 repliesA Paige AderholdThe smart ones will be set up in the Bermuda triangle with cameras etc to film the rocket falling back to earth!2w6Brooks Garner replied · 9 RepliesJack TuckerThey should play FLY Me To The Moon during lift off.2w5Nicole GrayEast of DeLand?
